findings.highlight: …I hate my outstanding ex-superior who set up this kind of culture.
findings.evidenceJa: …優秀な元上司が作り上げたこの文化が恨めしい。
findings.explanation: Haruki resents the workplace culture established by his excellent former superior, while the English directly says he hates the former superior.
findings.japanese: …優秀な元上司が作り上げたこの文化が恨めしい。
findings.todokanai: …I hate my outstanding ex-superior who set up this kind of culture.

findings.highlight: spent the whole night making love to Setsuna
findings.evidenceJa: 一晩中、雪菜と抱き合ったまま眠らずに
findings.explanation: Haruki stayed awake all night holding Setsuna in his arms. 抱き合ったまま means they remained in an embrace; it does not state that they had sex. 'Making love' invents a sexual act at a psychologically precise point in his accounting of sleepless nights.
findings.japanese:
そして、そのさらに前日は、
一晩中、雪菜と抱き合ったまま眠らずに…
findings.todokanai: And the day before that I spent the whole night making love to Setsuna, so I couldn't sleep then either…

findings.highlight: "Yeah, we can call it a celebration of your hard work. You even helped him out during this trip, so Kizaki-san's paying."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ほら、北原のお疲れ会ってことで。
今回の出張の事情のこともあるし、
全部木崎さん持ちで」
findings.explanation: Kizaki pays because of the circumstances surrounding this assignment; 'you even helped him out during this trip' invents a favor Haruki did Kizaki.
findings.japanese:
「ほら、北原のお疲れ会ってことで。
今回の出張の事情のこともあるし、
全部木崎さん持ちで」
findings.todokanai: "Yeah, we can call it a celebration of your hard work. You even helped him out during this trip, so Kizaki-san's paying."

findings.highlight: If they make me tell them about back then with alcohol involved, the regrets I've shut in the recesses of my mind will reappear.
findings.evidenceJa:
酒が入って、しかもあの時のことを語らされたら、
せっかく記憶の底に押し込めた後ろめたさが、
また蘇ってきてしまうから。
findings.explanation: 後ろめたさ is guilt, not regret; Haruki fears alcohol will revive his guilty conscience over choosing Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
酒が入って、しかもあの時のことを語らされたら、
せっかく記憶の底に押し込めた後ろめたさが、
また蘇ってきてしまうから。
findings.todokanai: If they make me tell them about back then with alcohol involved, the regrets I've shut in the recesses of my mind will reappear.

findings.highlight: neither a guardian angel nor a demon
findings.evidenceJa: 救いの神でも、地獄の仏でもなかった
findings.explanation: Both Japanese images are rescuers: a saving god and the proverbial Buddha encountered in hell. Hamada is neither kind of salvation from the drinking party. Turning the second into a demon changes the sentence to 'neither good nor evil' and loses the joke that Haruki has not been rescued at all.
findings.japanese:
そこに現れたのは、
どうやら救いの神でも、地獄の仏でもなかった。
findings.todokanai: The person who appeared was neither a guardian angel nor a demon.
